critical_code_review_comments: verify_unlock_otp records rate-limit fail attempts BEFORE reaching the 5-fail cap check (fails counted from login_attempts with 15min window). Correct semantics, but note: the 429 branch does NOT record a further attempt itself — a user who hits the cap stays capped for exactly 15min from their 5th fail, not sliding on 429 attempts. That's arguably the correct behaviour but worth documenting.

_consume_unlock_session correctly uses conditional update {uses_remaining>0, expires_at>now} to prevent negative decrement. Consider adding a $set to also clear the window when uses_remaining hits 0 (currently expires_at stays set but is inert). Purely cosmetic — no functional bug.

OTP invalidation on reissue uses update_many({used_at:null, invalidated_at:$exists:false}) which is idempotent, but relies on separate insert of the new OTP AFTER the invalidate. Under extreme race (two simultaneous issues), both new OTPs survive with the second invalidating the first, ending with one active. The comment (line ~955) explicitly documents this two-step ordering — good.

_cleanup_lock_refs_for_user with purge=True also deletes audit rows (KVKK erasure path). This is correct for GDPR-style purge; the hard mode keeps them (KVKK evidence). Distinction is well-documented but could benefit from a unit test for the purge path (only hard path tested here).

Rate-limit key 'otp:{tid}:{uid}' shares the login_attempts collection with actual login rate limiting. Fine, but if login-attempt cleanup jobs ever target 'identifier not containing colon' etc. they'd break OTP rate limiting silently.
